_note: The Singing School's townsfolk (decision 0434): Clarissa Sprague, Deacon Pratt, Hannah Corliss, Whipple, Rhoda Cobb, Fessenden, Widow Ames, Tom Nason and Submit Tolman. Each singer's last line sets their flag, then ss_enough once four of the six have said yes. Drafts for Matt or his writer friend.

lines.text: Sing from what? The books went into a box under the master's desk the winter the school stopped, and nobody's opened it since.
Including me. I'm not proud of it.
We filled that meetinghouse every winter. Then the man who led it stopped, and so did we. That's the town's fault, not his.
I'll be there, Mr. Burnbottom. Front pew. Don't look at me if you lose your place.
A singing school. On a weeknight. Led by that man.
Show me what you mean to sing, and I'll tell you if I'm coming.
He reads the printed parts through, every page, slowly.
Old Hundredth. Mear. Windham. These are hymns.
I'll come. Someone ought to see it's done decently.
One book won't do for a room. Leave it with me. I'll set the parts, every voice.
It'll take the day. Go and find somebody to hand them to.
Setting it now. Come back when you've found a few people to sing from them.
Thirty copies, every part. The ink's still wet. Don't hold them by the face.
I'll hear it from him. Not from you.
Burnbottom. Will you be sober?
I will.
Look at me when you say it.
I will, Phineas.
Then I'll come. I'll bring horehound, for after.
I can't sit still in a pew with my hands empty. I'd come if I had something to knit, and I'm out of wool.
Fessenden's got grey. He won't give it me on tick.
Wool, for Rhoda Cobb. To knit through the singing.
One skein. I've measured it twice. Tell her it's on the Reverend.
Grey. Good. I'll sit at the back where the Deacon can't see my needles.
I'd come. I can't climb that hill and then stand an hour at the top of it.
Unless somebody carries my chair. It's by my window.
Burnbottom, singing hymns, sober? Bring him in here and let me watch him say no to one. Then I'll come.
Tom Nason has the cup on the counter before Thadeous is through the door.
Your usual.
Thadeous looks at it a while.
Not tonight, Tom.
Well. That's the first time. I'll shut early and come and hear the second.
I'll come if he comes. Thirty years I've sat in that pew by myself, because he's up a tower.
He's coming down? Then I'm coming up.
You carry the chair up Meetinghouse Street and set it at the end of a pew, where she can see.
